key_terms: A commit strategy in which writers prepare updates without locks and the catalog accepts a commit only if the table state they observed is still current.
A condition sent with an Iceberg commit, such as the expected current snapshot or schema identity, that the catalog checks before swapping metadata.
An atomic update that replaces the current value only if it still equals an expected old value, the model behind a catalog's metadata pointer swap.
A rejected commit because another writer changed the table first. The client must reload and decide whether its operation is still valid.
A commit whose response was lost, so the client must check whether it succeeded before repeating a business append.

worked_examples.title: Reject a commit based on stale metadata
worked_examples.code:
from pyiceberg.exceptions import CommitFailedException
from pyiceberg.types import LongType

stale = catalog.load_table("demo.orders")
with table.update_schema() as update:
    update.add_column("note", LongType())
try:
    with stale.update_schema() as update:
        update.add_column("stale_field", LongType())
except CommitFailedException as error:
    print("rejected:", type(error).__name__)
worked_examples.interpretation: The second writer loaded the table before the note column existed, so its commit asserts a schema that is no longer current, and the SQL catalog refuses the pointer swap. The output names CommitFailedException. Silent success here would mean the catalog accepted a last-writer-wins update and lost note. The same check protects concurrent appends from replacing each other's snapshots.

worked_examples.title: Reload, revalidate and retry the intended change
worked_examples.code:
current = catalog.load_table("demo.orders")
names = current.schema().column_names
if "stale_field" not in names:
    with current.update_schema() as update:
        update.add_column("stale_field", LongType())
print(catalog.load_table("demo.orders").schema().column_names)
worked_examples.interpretation: The retry starts from freshly loaded metadata and checks whether its change is still needed before committing, so the final column list contains id, region, amount, note and stale_field. Blindly retrying the old update object would fail again, and retrying a data append without revalidation can double write rows. Decide per operation whether a conflict should retry, merge or stop for a human.

worked_examples.title: Inspect the metadata pointer after each commit
worked_examples.code:
print(catalog.load_table("demo.orders").metadata_location)
with current.update_schema() as update:
    update.add_column("reviewed", LongType())
print(catalog.load_table("demo.orders").metadata_location)
worked_examples.interpretation: Each line prints a different metadata JSON path under the table metadata directory, with an incremented version prefix. The SQL catalog row stores only this pointer, so a commit is a compare-and-swap on that row. When diagnosing a conflict, compare the location a writer loaded with the current one; if they differ, the writer was stale.

evidence: Complete actual local program with independent expected values and explicit negative checks; distributed-system claims are excluded.
